web/composer/planner_authoring_aids.py:R: R1 `dict(snapshot.selected_profile_aliases).get(llm_id)`. The receiver is NOT external data: `snapshot` is `PluginAvailabilitySnapshot`, an ELSPETH-owned frozen dataclass (`web/plugin_policy/models.py`). The finding is nonetheless correct to surface and wrong to remove, because that type encodes plugin->alias as a PARTIAL pair list whose value is itself optional: `selected_profile_aliases: tuple[tuple[PluginId, str | None], ...]`. A plugin the operator never gave a profile selection contributes NO pair; a plugin whose selection was cleared contributes `(plugin_id, None)`. Both spell the same fact -- 'this deployment has selected no alias for this plugin' -- so the membership rewrite is NOT equivalent here: `llm_id in mapping` is True for the explicit-None case that must still fall through. `.get()` collapsing both shapes to None is the honest reading of the field's own type. What it protects: the aid must teach this deployment's real operator profile alias or fall back to its first usable one, never invent an alias name. The fallback on the next line, `dict(snapshot.usable_profile_aliases)[llm_id][0]`, is deliberately a REQUIRED-key subscript -- `llm_id` was taken from that same tuple four statements above, so a snapshot that is genuinely inconsistent still crashes; only the documented 'nothing selected' fact is defaulted.

R1 `dict(snapshot.control_modes).get(capability, ControlMode.RECOMMEND)`. Tier-1/2 owned data (`PluginAvailabilitySnapshot.control_modes: tuple[tuple[PluginCapability, ControlMode], ...]`), but the tuple is explicitly partial: `PluginAvailabilitySnapshot.create` defaults `control_modes=()`, and `for_trained_operator` constructs a snapshot with none at all, so an unlisted capability is the NORMAL state of a deployment that has configured no control policy for it. `ControlMode.RECOMMEND` is not an invented default -- it is the policy default the control model is built on, and the direction is fail-safe in the sense that matters here: reading absent policy as RECOMMEND can only make the worked exemplar OMIT a control node, never make it wire a control this deployment never selected. Reading absence as REQUIRED (or raising) would teach the planner a topology whose coverage validator this deployment does not run. The whole function is guarded by this one test and returns None for every non-REQUIRED case.

R1 `dict(snapshot.selected).get(capability)`. Same two-shaped absence as `selected_profile_aliases`, on a different field: `selected: tuple[tuple[PluginCapability, PluginId | None], ...]`. `PluginAvailabilitySnapshot.for_trained_operator` emits `(capability, min(plugin_ids) if plugin_ids else None)` for EVERY member of `PluginCapability`, so a capability with no admitted implementation is present-with-None; a capability the availability pass never considered is absent. Both mean 'no plugin selected for this capability', and the `if plugin_id is None: return None` immediately below routes both to the same correct outcome -- the aid teaches manual wiring rather than naming a control. A membership-form read would treat the present-with-None case as a selection and go on to look up a profile alias for `None`.

R1 `dict(snapshot.selected_profile_aliases).get(plugin_id)`. Same field and same argument as the `_usable_llm_profile_alias` site: `str | None` values over a partial pair list mean absence is expressible two ways, so `.get()` is the only read that treats them alike. Here the None result is not an error but a documented first-class case named in this function's own docstring -- a required control selected WITHOUT operator profile aliases is a direct user-configurable control, returned as `(plugin_id.name, None)` so the exemplar still carries the required node. Raising on the missing pair would make every deployment whose required control is direct-config unable to render its worked exemplar at all.

R1 `dict(snapshot.usable_profile_aliases).get(plugin_id, ())`. `usable_profile_aliases: tuple[tuple[PluginId, tuple[str, ...]], ...]` carries a pair only for plugins that HAVE an operator profile projection; a direct-config control (`web/plugin_policy/profiles.py` builds profile views only for profiled plugins) contributes no pair at all. The `()` default IS that documented case rather than a papered-over lookup failure, and the very next expression, `alias = aliases[0] if aliases else None`, consumes it as such -- an empty alias set and an absent one are the same fact and produce the same `alias=None` that the docstring specifies. This read is reached only after the `alias is None` branch above has already established that no alias was explicitly selected.

R6 `except ValueError:` around `catalog.get_schema(kind, pair[1])`. This handler does not swallow: it records a NAMED, typed omission and continues -- `omission_candidates.append({"plugin_id": label, "reason": "schema_unavailable"})`, an `_SchemaContractEvidenceOmission` row that `_schema_evidence_envelope` publishes to the planner alongside `omissions_withheld_count`, so the gap is disclosed in the evidence envelope rather than lost. The rule cannot see that channel because the handler neither raises nor returns. Control by symbol: `_schema_evidence_envelope` (envelope assembly, which carries `omitted` and the withheld count) and `_schema_pair_label` (the identity naming the omission). Re-raising is wrong at this seam: the function rehydrates whole current contracts for a SET of previously discovered plugin identities, and one plugin whose schema is unavailable under the CURRENT policy must not abort the carry-forward for the others -- that would let a single rotated-out plugin blank the planner's entire schema-contract evidence. Unavailability is an ordinary policy fact here, already reported through this same omission channel by the sibling `pair not in available` and `_SCHEMA_EVIDENCE_MAX_ENTRIES` arms. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/composer/test_schema_contract_carry_forward.py::test_final_envelope_stays_within_byte_budget_after_withheld_count_growth`, whose fake catalog raises `ValueError("schema_unavailable")`.

R6 `except _SchemaContractProjectionUnsupported:` around `planner_plugin_contract(schema)`. Same disclosure channel as the handler above, with a different reason literal: `omission_candidates.append({"plugin_id": label, "reason": "schema_projection_unsupported"})`. The caught exception is not an anomaly but this file's own deliberate refusal signal -- `_contract_json_schema`, `_contract_discriminator` and `_contract_knob_schema` raise it by design for any plugin fragment outside the closed projected vocabulary, and `planner_plugin_contract` raises it again for a bare boolean schema or a projection over `_PLANNER_CONTRACT_MAX_CANONICAL_BYTES`. Control by symbol: `_schema_evidence_envelope` publishes the omission with its reason, and the caller reopens the gap from it. Re-raising would invert the design -- one third-party plugin with an unprojectable ConfigModel would deny every OTHER plugin's contract to the planner. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/composer/test_schema_contract_carry_forward.py::test_unknown_nonprose_schema_keyword_omits_whole_contract_and_reopens_gap`, which asserts the exact omitted row this handler writes.

R1 `public_schema.knob_schema.get("fields", ())`. Tier-3: `knob_schema` is a third-party plugin's ConfigModel lowered by `web/catalog/knob_schema` and then projected by `PluginProfileProjection`, which is exactly why this same payload type gets a raising `@trust_boundary` (`_contract_knob_schema`) on the admission path. This site is NOT that admission path -- it is the discovery digest, which publishes `required_options` for every profiled plugin in one catalog sweep on every planner call. Absence is read in the conservative direction only: no `fields` key yields an empty public-required list, so the digest simply carries no `required_options` for that entry. That can only UNDER-claim what the deployment demands; it can never invent a required option the planner would then be told to fill, and the authoritative requirement is enforced later by `set_pipeline` prevalidation regardless. Hardening this into a raise would let one plugin's odd lowering abort the discovery digest every planner call depends on.

R1 `field.get("required")` in the same comprehension. Same Tier-3 payload and same conservative direction: a lowered field entry that declares no `required` key is read as not-required, which can only shrink the published `required_options` set, never grow it. The contrast on this very line is deliberate and load-bearing: `field["name"]` is a REQUIRED-key subscript, because a knob field with no name is a genuine contract break in ELSPETH's own lowering rather than an optional plugin declaration, and it crashes rather than publishing a nameless required option. So the defensiveness here is scoped precisely to the two keys a plugin may legitimately omit, and the one key ELSPETH guarantees is read as a member.

R1 `_AIDS_MEMO.get(key)` -- the first, uncontended cache read under `_AIDS_MEMO_LOCK`. `_AIDS_MEMO: dict[str, _PlannerAuthoringAids]` is a module-private bounded memo (Tier-1, never external), keyed by `f"{catalog.snapshot.snapshot_hash}:{catalog_source}:{catalog_sha256}"` -- an UNBOUNDED key space, since every policy rotation and every OpenRouter catalog re-prime mints a fresh key. A missing key is therefore not a broken contract but the cache MISS this function exists to service, and `if cached is None:` on the next line is that miss handler, which runs the full `_build_planner_authoring_aids` catalog sweep. The None is unambiguous: the only write is `_AIDS_MEMO[key] = cached = built`, so a stored value is never None and `.get()`'s None means 'not cached' and nothing else.

R1 `_AIDS_MEMO.get(key)` -- the second read, the double-checked lookup taken after the ~50ms catalog sweep has completed and the lock has been re-acquired. Missing is not merely tolerable here, it is the EXPECTED outcome: this read exists solely to discover the rarer case that another worker populated the same snapshot key while this one was building, so that the losing builder defers to the stored value instead of evicting and replacing it. A required-key read would turn the normal, uncontended path -- nobody else wrote the key -- into a KeyError on every cold build. Same Tier-1 module-private memo and same unambiguous None as the first read; the bounded eviction (`_AIDS_MEMO_MAX`) immediately below runs only on that miss.

R1 `dict(catalog.snapshot.selected).get(PluginCapability.PROMPT_SHIELD)` inside the `selected_shield :=` walrus. Same owned partial pair list with optional values as the `_selected_control_profile` selection read (`selected: tuple[tuple[PluginCapability, PluginId | None], ...]`), so absent-pair and present-with-None are the same 'this deployment selected no prompt shield' fact and must read alike. This site differs from `_selected_control_profile` in one respect that makes the `.get()` necessary rather than incidental: it reads the selection REGARDLESS of control mode, because the prompt-shield rules must name whichever shield THIS deployment selected (aws_bedrock_prompt_shield, azure_prompt_shield, ...) and never a hardcoded vendor. The walrus falsy arm passes `shield_plugin=None`, which is what makes `_prompt_shield_rules` render vendor-neutral guidance instead of fabricating a plugin name -- the exact failure this indirection exists to prevent.

R1 `control_modes.get(PluginCapability.PROMPT_SHIELD, ControlMode.RECOMMEND) is ControlMode.REQUIRED`. `control_modes` is the locally built `dict(catalog.snapshot.control_modes)` over the same partial, `()`-defaulting owned tuple as the `_selected_control_profile` mode read, and the same reasoning applies: a deployment that configured no control mode for PROMPT_SHIELD has no pair, and RECOMMEND is the policy default rather than an invented value. The consequence here is purely in taught prose -- the boolean only selects whether the rules tell the planner the shield is required or recommended -- and the fail-safe direction is to under-claim: an unset policy must never make the aid instruct the planner that a control is mandatory when this deployment's admission gate will not demand it.
